text: Insect specimen collection, University of Edinburgh 1823: Butterfly pinned to display board continues laying eggs. Eggs hatch into butterflies that immediately fly into past tense. Collection case now contains 847 identical specimens from s

Personal diary, housewife in Toledo 1955: The shadows in my kitchen point toward tomorrow instead of away from the sun. Made coffee using tomorrow's shadow it tastes like regret and knows things I haven't done yet.
Census record, Pompeii 78 CE: Lists family of four plus the man who arrives every Thursday to warn us. Enumerator notes subject speaks only future tense, wears clothing that hasn't been invented yet.

Medical examiner's report, Boston 1892: Autopsy reveals deceased's heart contains fully formed pocket watch keeping accurate time. Watch face displays date of patient's birth. Mechanism appears to be counting backward to zero.

Municipal water records, Phoenix 1973: Resident complaints of tap water tasting like childhood summers. Chemical analysis confirms H2O contains trace amounts of bicycle bells, scraped knees, and the exact temperature of grandmother's kitche

Archaeological survey, Çatalhöyük 6500 BCE: Settlement layout matches Manhattan street grid with 97 accuracy. Excavated hearths align perfectly with subway stations that won't exist for 8,000 years. No explanation in site notes.

Weather station data, Reykjavik 1987: Barometric pressure readings spell out complete sonnet when plotted chronologically. Poem describes storm that occurred three days before instruments detected it. Meteorologist's notes redacted by unkno

Geological survey, Yellowstone 1934: Thermal vent releases steam containing fragments of conversations that won't occur until 2089. Recorded samples include accurate stock predictions and three marriage proposals between people not yet born

Personnel file, East India Company 1742: Clerk recorded as having died of nostalgia for places that do not exist. Death certificate signed by physician who won't be born until 1823. Clerk's position remains officially unfilled.

Census data, Roman Britain 212 CE: Population count includes 847 residents listed as temporarily elsewhere when. Enumerators noted subjects were physically present but experientially absent. Column for when left blank in all cases.

Dream journal recovered from Pompeii ash, 79 CE: Final entry describes escaping the eruption via subway system. Detailed map of underground tunnels matches 1884 London plans exactly. Journal owner died in house.

Autopsy report, Vienna 1902: Subject died of temporal displacement syndrome. Internal organs aged at different rates heart from 1902, lungs from 1847, liver from 1923. Coroner noted patient was still breathing during examination.

Archaeological report: Pleistocene site, 40,000 BCE, contains Neanderthal burial with grave goods including obsidian blade, mammoth ivory, and laminated employee ID badge from Blockbuster Video. Badge expires 2004.

Personal diary, merchant's widow, Lübeck 1456: The stars rearranged themselves to spell my late husband's name. Lasted three nights. Astronomers insist no such configuration occurred. I have witnesses.

Botanical survey, Amazon basin 1889: Vine specimens collected exhibited temporal growth rings spanning centuries within hours. Pressed samples aged backward in herbarium. Original collector found saplings he planted had become ancient trees
